prompt:
Create one premium product illustration for the welcome/onboarding panel of Falcon, a professional QA test management application. This is a decorative product collage, not a screenshot or evidence.

Canvas: wide horizontal 2.06:1 aspect ratio, edge-to-edge dark charcoal (#111111 to #191919), suitable for an inset displayed around 350 by 170 CSS pixels. The composition must be crisp and readable at that small size. Fill the useful width with a carefully composed collage, without vast dead space.

Art direction: understated, meticulous enterprise software editorial image; the restrained dark materials, thin warm-gray dividers, small rounded controls, clean white/light-gray text hierarchy and elegant line icons of a modern Linear-like workspace. Nearly monochrome with only a few soft blue selection accents and green success dots. No purple gradients, no neon glows, no large 3D symbols, no mascots, no people, no photos, no fake logos, no watermark.

Composition: three overlapping slightly tilted desktop UI panels in a gentle three-quarter perspective, layered with soft realistic shadows. A large rear panel spans most of the width with a narrow vertical icon rail, a well-spaced folder tree with thin curved connecting lines on the left, and a concise test-case editor on the right. In front at the lower right, a smaller execution results panel with three or four tidy list rows and quiet green checkmarks. A small secondary folder-structure panel peeks out at the upper left. Rounded top corners on panels, matte graphite frames, precise spacing. The panels should look related to the supplied Falcon screenshot's neutral dark interface, never like a generic analytics dashboard. Render actual folder-line icons and checklist rows rather than decorative charts.

Text: keep tiny text sparse and nonessential; use only short clear headings such as "Test cases", "Folders", "Scenario", and "Results". Do not put greeting text in the illustration: the application will overlay a localized greeting later. Avoid large text, trial messaging, payment messaging, or buttons outside the miniature panels. Keep the image polished, calm, contemporary and intentionally art-directed.
